title: Priority ladder and autoscale contract for heterogeneous GPU fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Create an intake-to-decision contract for enterprise dedicated requests that have mixed GPU families and strict SLOs. We need a deterministic prioritization ladder, an autoscale budget 'contract' that specifies guaranteed reserved throughput versus burst allowances, and a GPU selection policy that minimizes noisy-neighbor risk while meeting latency targets. Background: Sales/CS sees multiple incoming requests from enterprise customers that require reserved capacity across NVidia A100/RTX/TrnX families and want both guaranteed TPS and headroom for bursts. Current intake is ad-hoc; ENG needs clear constraints to size pools and propose fallbacks. Scope: This ticket covers intake questionnaire additions, the prioritization ladder logic, autoscale contract templates (guaranteed vs burstable bands), and the guidance for GPU-class assignment. It does NOT include implementation of autoscale enforcement in the runtime or billing system (separate ENG work). Success criteria: (1) Intake form updated and published; (2) Playbook with decision matrix that PMs/SEs can use to produce a recommended pool configuration for 90% of enterprise asks; (3) A short policy template that legal/finance can include in reserved contracts; (4) Engineering acceptance of the sizing heuristics.
decision_log: 2025-02-18: Chose a three-band priority ladder (Critical / Production / Development) rather than percentiles to keep stakeholder language consistent with sales tiers.
2025-02-21: Opted for a two-tier autoscale contract: Guaranteed (reserved) throughput + Burst Credits ledger (time-windowed) instead of soft burst absolute limits.
2025-02-25: GPU selection policy will prefer same-generation GPUs for guaranteed capacity and allow mixed-fleet burst nodes; engineering validated impact on KV cache locality for mixed fleets.
2025-02-28: Decided to expose estimated tail-latency delta to customers for each GPU class in the intake response PDF to set expectations.
acceptance_criteria: Updated intake form published in Confluence and linked from the sales SE toolkit.
Playbook accepted by runtime engineering (ENG) with signed-off heuristics for sizing and fallback ladders.
Two autoscale contract templates (Standard enterprise and High-availability) drafted and reviewed by Legal and Finance.
A set of 5 example customer requests mapped to recommended pool configs that match existing historical telemetry within +/-20% of observed peak throughput.
QA checklist for handoff to ENG implementation created and assigned.
tasks: Draft intake form questions for throughput, p95/p99 latency targets, burst patterns, job type (sync vs async), and tolerance for degradations
Run telemetry pull to map 30 representative enterprise workloads to GPU family performance (ENG help)
Create priority ladder decision matrix and numeric scoring rules
Draft autoscale contract language and burst credits definition for Legal
Review GPU-assignment guidance with Runtime team and add constraints for KV cache locality
Publish playbook and schedule 1-hour training for SEs and onboarding PMs
